title: Abundance answers the taunt of being “cut off”

phrase.meaning: the one who hates you is the one cut off

points.label: What research comes close
points.text: **Ibn Kathir** gathers reports that enemies called the Prophet **abtar**, “cut off” from heirs, when his sons died; al-Suddī says they thought his remembrance would end. Ibn Kathir replies that God **preserved his remembrance**, and the hater is the one forgotten.

points.label: One possible reading
points.text: The surah sets **kawthar**, “abundance”, against **abtar**, “cut off”, joined by the same -ar rhyme and the same “you”. The one mocked as lacking is named the one **given much**; prayer and sacrifice in the middle are how the gift is **received**.

bottom_text: This is one reading. Ibn Kathir’s reports name four different enemies, so the heirs story may be read into the word; the surah itself never mentions sons.
source_label: Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur’an al-‘Azim, Surah 108
